- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant clarified that they do not have a physical presence and did not have a still-life setup in a park with the user.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for getting started with watercolor painting, including:
  1. Choose the right paper (hot press or cold press).
  2. Select your paints (tubes or pans).
  3. Invest in good brushes (natural hair or synthetic).
  4. Understand the basics of color theory.
  5. Start with simple exercises (wet-on-wet, wet-on-dry, glazing).
  6. Use reference images.
  7. Practice regularly.
  8. Work from light to dark.
  9. Use the white of the paper.
  10. Have fun.
- [USER] The user acknowledged the tip about paper.
- [USER] The user asked for recommendations for a specific brand of watercolor paper suitable for beginners.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended several brands of watercolor paper for beginners:
  1. Winsor & Newton Cotman series.
  2. Arches 140lb cold press paper.
  3. Strathmore 500 Series Watercolor Paper.
  4. Canson Mi-Teintes and XL series.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised to look for paper that is 140lb (300gsm) or heavier, acid-free, and to choose a size that feels comfortable.
